Job Title: Project Manager, Large Projects CMD Commercial Job Location: Remote, California, United States of America Job Location Type: Remote Job Contract Type: Full time Job Seniority Level: Work Schedule: 40 hours per week Work Schedule First Shift (Days) Environmental Conditions Office Job Description Job Description As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale.

Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer.

We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.

DESCRIPTION: At Thermo Fisher Scientific, you'll manage complex strategic projects that make a meaningful impact on our mission to enable customers to make the world healthier, cleaner, and safer.

As Sr Project Manager, you'll guide successful execution of important initiatives across functions, ensuring timely delivery, risk mitigation, and stakeholder alignment.

You'll manage multiple high-priority projects simultaneously, coordinating cross-functional teams through the complete project lifecycle while maintaining focus on business objectives and quality standards.

Your expertise will be instrumental in implementing process improvements, new technologies, and transformational changes that enhance operational efficiency and customer success.

Project Manager – Large Projects Administrative Project Management Focus Position Summary The Project Manager – Large Projects is responsible for the administrative coordination, governance, documentation, tracking, and reporting required to support large, complex projects.

This role ensures that project information is organized, timelines are visible, actions are tracked, risks and issues are documented, and stakeholders have accurate information to support decision-making. This role does not own solution design, deployment strategy, customer adoption, operational readiness, or business execution.

Instead, the Project Manager provides the structure, cadence, documentation, and administrative discipline needed to keep large projects organized and transparent.

This is an individual contributor role that works closely with project sponsors, workstream owners, Solution Deployment Leaders, commercial teams, operations, finance, legal, quality, supply chain, digital, and other stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities: Project Administration and Coordination Maintain project plans, timelines, milestones, action trackers, decision logs, risk logs, issue logs, and dependency trackers. Coordinate project meetings, governance forums, steering committee reviews, and stakeholder update sessions.

Prepare meeting agendas, capture minutes, document decisions, and follow up on assigned actions. Ensure project documentation is complete, current, organized, and accessible to appropriate stakeholders. Support consistent use of project templates, tools, trackers, and reporting formats.

Governance Support Support project governance by maintaining meeting cadence, escalation records, approval documentation, and decision history. Track required approvals, sign-offs, stage gates, and governance checkpoints. Ensure project sponsors and workstream owners have accurate information for reviews and decisions.

Maintain visibility to open decisions, overdue actions, unresolved issues, and upcoming milestones. Help ensure governance processes are followed consistently across large projects. Timeline and Milestone Tracking Maintain the master project timeline based on input from workstream owners and accountable business leads.

Track progress against milestones, deliverables, and agreed due dates. Identify and flag timeline variances, overdue items, and dependency gaps for review by accountable owners. Consolidate updates from multiple workstreams into a single project view. Support visibility to critical path items without owning execution of the underlying work.

Reporting and Communication Support Prepare project status reports, dashboards, executive summaries, and stakeholder updates. Consolidate inputs from workstream owners, deployment leaders, finance, operations, commercial teams, and other functions.

Ensure project reports clearly reflect status, milestones, risks, issues, decisions needed, and next steps. Maintain accurate records of project communications and leadership updates. Support consistent and timely information flow across project stakeholders. Risk, Issue, and Action Tracking Maintain risk, issue, action, and dependency logs.

Document risk descriptions, issue status, owners, target dates, mitigation updates, and escalation history. Follow up with accountable owners to obtain updates and closure status. Flag overdue actions, unresolved issues, or missing information to project sponsors or designated leads.

Support escalation documentation but does not own resolution of technical, operational, commercial, or deployment issues. Budget and Resource Administration Track project budget information, purchase orders, invoices, resource assumptions, and financial updates as directed by finance or project sponsors.

Consolidate budget and resource inputs for project reporting. Maintain documentation related to project spend, approvals, forecasts, and financial decisions. Support administrative coordination of vendor documentation, contracts, statements of work, and related records.

Flag missing financial information, pending approvals, or budget variances for review by accountable owners. Documentation and Records Management Maintain organized project repositories, files, version control, and document naming standards.

Ensure key project documents, approvals, meeting records, reports, and governance materials are stored appropriately. Support audit readiness by maintaining clear records of decisions, approvals, risks, changes, and status updates. Capture lessons learned and archive project materials at project close.

Support continuous improvement of project administration tools, templates, and documentation practices. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in business, operations, project management, life sciences, engineering, or related field preferred.

Experience supporting large projects, complex initiatives, project management offices, commercial operations, business operations, or administrative project coordination. Strong skills in project documentation, meeting coordination, status reporting, action tracking, and records management.

Ability to consolidate information from multiple stakeholders into clear, accurate project updates. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. Ability to manage multiple deadlines, documents, trackers, and reporting cycles. Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Proficiency with project management, collaboration, reporting, and productivity tools. Ability to work in a matrixed organization and follow up with stakeholders across functions and levels. Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting large customer, commercial, operational, supply chain, digital, or transformation projects.

Experience in life sciences, pharmaceutical, biopharma, healthcare, diagnostics, laboratory, manufacturing, or regulated environments. Familiarity with project governance, PMO practices, stage-gate processes, and executive reporting.

Experience with tools such as Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, Teams, Power BI, CRM, ERP, or similar platforms. Understanding of budget tracking, purchase order processes, vendor documentation, or contract administration. Project management certification or training preferred but not required.

Key Competencies Project administration Documentation management Meeting coordination Status reporting Timeline tracking Action-item follow-up Risk and issue logging Governance support Records management Attention to detail Stakeholder follow-up Tool and tracker discipline Scope and Impact The Project Manager – Large Projects is an individual contributor role focused on the administrative management of large, complex projects.

The role supports project transparency, governance discipline, documentation quality, leadership visibility, and timely follow-up. The role does not own solution deployment, customer adoption, operational readiness, business execution, technical solution design, or commercial strategy.

Accountability for those activities remains with designated business owners, Solution Deployment Leaders, Solution Architects, commercial leaders, and functional teams. Travel Requirements Limited travel may be required for project meetings, governance sessions, workshops, or site-based coordination.

Compensation and Benefits The salary range estimated for this position based in California is $112,500.00–$168,500.00. This position may also be eligible to receive a variable annual bonus based on company, team, and/or individual performance results in accordance with company policy.

You will serve as the government lead of the Release Assembly Integrated Product Team for the W93/Mk7 portfolio to ensure the coordinated delivery of key subsystems to the program.
You will represent the Reentry Systems branch at the Accuracy Improvement Program and Future Mission Equipment working groups, supporting rapid deployment of new technologies to programs of record.
You will draft and manage the technical and programmatic scope of relevant contractual vehicles in support of the Reentry Systems portfolio, including work requests, task orders, and Military Interdepartmental Procurement Requests (MIPR).
You will lead the management and coordination of a diverse staff of federal civilian, military, industry/contractor, and other government agency efforts to deliver mission success.
You will closely coordinate with the staff of other sections and units within the Reentry Systems Branch to ensure delivery of excellence across the technical and programmatic spectrum.
You will independently highlight and resolve issues affecting their equities; directs and participates in reviews of progress and/or issues with Reentry Branch staff members and other stakeholders.
You will communicates the status of progress regularly with Unit, Section, and Branch leadership.
You will partner with various stakeholders, such as National Nuclear Security Administration, United States Air Force, and Federally Funded Research and Development Centers.
You will formulate and execute requirements, planning factors, and budgets necessary to support design, development, production, and test and evaluation of the Navy's reentry systems portfolio.
Your resume must also demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the NH-02 (GS-11) grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector.

Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: Applying knowledge of engineering concepts, methods, and practices relevant to reentry and nuclear weapon applications to plan, schedule, budget, and coordinate highly complex technical efforts in support of mission objectives.

Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management website: For the 0801/0830/0861/0893 series: All Professional Engineering Positions, 0800 For the 1310 series: Physics Series 1310 For the 1320 series: Chemistry Series, 1320 For the 1501 series: General Mathematics and Statistics Series 1501 Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

Oversees support functions and coordinating with teams and industry contractors to resolve end-user issues.
Manages the full lifecycle of IT projects for approximately 52,000 customers, including requirement capture, project planning, execution, and quality assurance.
Validates customer IT requirements, assisting with equipment procurement, and coordinating project cost capturing and billing.
Provides prioritized IT support for senior-ranking officials, special projects, and resolving difficult or complex local area network problems.
Serves as the Branch property hand receipt holder and utilizing the Defense Property Accountability System (DPAS) to inventory and manage government IT assets.
Basic Requirements: Applicants must have IT-related experience demonstrating the following competencies appropriate to, or above, the level of this position. For vacancies below the full-performance level of the position, the basic requirement will be evaluated on a developmental basis.

Your resume and work experience should clearly support your ability to meet these competencies and will be evaluated as part of the entire application process.

Attention to Detail - Experience reviewing my own information technology-related work or data and have been responsible for reviewing the work of others to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency with standards.

Customer Service-Developing and maintaining relationships with customers, anticipating and assessing the current and future information technology needs of customers, and developing or identifying information technology products or services that are tailored to meet customer needs Oral Communication-Briefing senior-level management and IT staff on the status of information technology systems, projects, or daily operations, including the communication of complex technical information to a non-technical audience Problem Solving-Identifying alternatives to address unique, highly complex, or sensitive information technology-related issues.

I have anticipated information technology-related problems and have identified and evaluated potential sources of information to generate alternative solutions. Qualifying Experience: To qualify at the GG-12, your resume must describe at least one year of experience that demonstrates the competencies necessary for immediate success in the position.

Experience refers to any paid or unpaid experience, including volunteer work and Military service, that would be considered equivalent to work normally performed at the next lower grade level in the federal service.

For this position, qualifying experience is defined as: Supporting operations, managing the full life-cycle of IT projects, facilitating IT equipment and services procurement, cost capturing, billing, and maintaining accountability of government property; in addition to IT related experience demonstrating Attention to Detail, Customer Service, Oral Communication, and Problem Solving as described in the vacancy announcement.

Candidates must describe how they meet the qualifying experience and/or selective placement factor(s) within the body of their resume. All qualifications must be met within 30 days after the closing date of this announcement.

1. Provides group level direction and management for work characterized as infrastructure support for organizations and tenants of the host ANG base.

Directs work to be accomplished by an organization consisting of 8 - 12 full-time direct-report subordinate supervisors and 100-150 base support employees in technician grades up to GS-13, Active Guard/Reserve (AGR) military grades up to Lt Colonel, and various state program and contract employees engaged in supervisory, professional, technical and administrative work.

The base level of work managed and directed is determined to be GS-11.

Directs and supervises, through subordinate supervisors, staff and production functions affecting base operating support through a wide variety of high cost, sophisticated communications and computer systems, personnel data systems, real property assets, and associated equipment that comprise a significant share of base fiscal resources. 2.

Implements the host Mission Support Group portion of the Designed Operational Capability (DOC) statement of the unit and/or the Emergency War Orders (EWO).

In support of USAF Air Expeditionary Force (AEF), Expeditionary Combat Support (ECS) requirements, develops and implements unit plans for execution of deployments and contingency objectives to meet USAF and Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) goals.

Coordinates required AEF planning and resources with other ANG and USAF units, the National Guard Bureau, and other higher headquarters agencies to support and implement the AEF mission. Represents the wing at scheduled national-level planning conferences to commit wing personnel and materiel resources to sustain AEF/ECS tasking.

Through analysis of unit strengths and capabilities, balances ECS commitments to ensure acceptable OPSTEMPO and PERSTEMPO levels. Manages and directs all wing activation, mobilization, deployment, and demobilization activities and functions.

Represents and speaks for the Wing Commander in the designated jurisdictional area with representatives of the National Guard Bureau, the Adjutant General, USP&FO, MAJCOMs, other military components, tenant units and organizations, state/local governments, local media, business and other public/private groups or organizations having an interest in the programs of the wing/base. 3.

Directs the unit Status of Resources and Training Systems (SORTS) and AEF Reporting Tool (ART) reports for all mission support functions to reflect unit mission capability under wartime conditions. Identifies training, personnel, and equipment requirements, and ensures the readiness capability of each assigned unit.

Assesses the status impact on organizational programs and resource management. Serves as primary advisor to the wing staff concerning application and implementation of new technologies that affect host base operations.

Maintains awareness of technological advances and oversees application and implementation of high technology issues and developments associated with command, control, communications, and computers (C4), personnel data systems, air base operability, and security systems. 4.

Oversees the management and direction of the host Mission Support and Military Personnel Flights. Directs the development and implementation of local military personnel policies and procedures.

Through supervision of the Director of Personnel, plans, organizes, directs and controls wing military personnel programs, to include initial accession, education, training, and assignment to appropriate military specialties. Coordinates full-time personnel policies and programs with the state Human Resources Office (HRO).

Ensures equal employment opportunity and diversity program elements are established and implemented within the wing. Monitors base recruiting and retention programs to ensure effective work force objectives are met. Ensures the host Mission Support Flight is organized, trained and equipped for worldwide contingency deployment. 5.

Oversees base wide logistics readiness functions, to include supply, transportation/traffic management, vehicle operations and maintenance, fuels management, and logistics plans and programs, to ensure the primary peacetime and wartime flying mission of the wing/base is supported at all times.

Ensures logistics resources are available to meet flying mission and base support requirements through active participation and involvement in budget planning and acquisition/maintenance of facilities, manpower, vehicles, fuels, technical data, munitions, tools, supplies, and related support equipment.

In coordination with the Aircraft Maintenance Group Commander, sets policy, directs, and monitors base level support and related programs in compliance with Defense Management Review (DMR) 904 for supply and repair of aircraft parts and components. Performs other duties as assigned. PLEASE CONTACT HRO FOR COMPLETE POSITION DESCRIPTION.

If you are not sure you are eligible for military membership, please contact an Alabama Air National Guard recruiter at (800) 864-6264 prior to applying for this position.

Why this role exists: The purpose of this role is to deliver consistent team outputs and outcomes through predictable execution, operational efficiency, and people performance within a single team.

The role directly contributes to stream -level business value by ensuring the team reliably produces high-quality deliverables aligned with stream priorities. It combines delivery ownership with people leadership to build a sustainable, high-performing team capable of growing with business demands. What you’ll drive:
Delivery ownership and execution

Own predictable, on-time delivery within the team, balancing speed, quality, and sustainability.
Track delivery progress, manage end-to-end initiatives, handle ambiguous requirements, and address risks, blockers, and dependencies.
Partner with Head of Stream , Tech Lead, and Product Managers to align priorities, technical standards, and scope trade-offs.
Provide regular visibility into team progress, risks, and trade-offs to stakeholders.

Process improvement and quality assurance

Continuously improve team delivery processes, reducing friction, bottlenecks, and the cost of change.
Ensure team compliance with operational standards, SLA adherence, and adoption of stream -level processes and AI-driven solutions.
Own deliverable quality for reliability, performance, and maintainability, ensuring capacity is allocated for technical debt reduction in collaboration with Tech Lead.

People leadership and team development

Directly manage team members, conduct 1:1s, own the performance cycle, set clear goals, and execute PDPs.
Drive team engagement, psychological safety, collaboration, knowledge sharing, and onboarding.
Participate in the hiring process by defining team needs, interviewing, and making hiring recommendations.

Resource and capacity management

Optimize team capacity, workload distribution, and on-call rotations to maximize throughput and prevent burnout.
Own team-level capacity planning and flag resource gaps to the Head of Stream .

3+ years of experience in engineering delivery management and people leadership, including direct management of a software development team in a product or platform environment.
Practical project and delivery management expertise with adaptable methodologies.
Understanding of team-level resource planning and capacity management.
Familiarity with engineering practices, CI/CD, and quality assurance processes.
Ability to work with data and metrics to drive decisions and improve performance.
Strong stakeholder management and cross-team coordination skills across product, engineering, and delivery teams.

The successful candidate will take clear ownership of complex delivery outcomes, ensuring strategic priorities are aligned, cross-team dependencies are managed, and measurable value is consistently realised across services and platforms.

## Abteilungsleitung Offene Jugendarbeit Zentrum ##
Ihre neue Rolle
Sie übernehmen die personelle, fachliche, organisatorische und finanzielle Führung der Offenen Jugendarbeit Zentrum und gestalten deren Weiterentwicklung aktiv mit. Gemeinsam mit dem Team sorgen Sie für eine zeitgemässe, bedarfsgerechte und zukunftsorientierte Ausrichtung der Offenen Jugendarbeit in der Stadt St.Gallen.
Als Mitglied der Geschäftsleitung der Dienststelle Kinder Jugend Familie bringen Sie jugendrelevante Themen ein, wirken an strategischen Entscheidungen mit und vertreten die Anliegen von Jugendlichen und jungen Erwachsenen innerhalb der städtischen Strukturen.
Gleichzeitig bleiben Sie nah an der Praxis: Sie arbeiten bei Bedarf in den verschiedenen Angeboten der Offenen Jugendarbeit Zentrum mit, begleiten Projekte und Aktionen gemeinsam mit Jugendlichen und unterstützen Ihr Team in der Umsetzung innovativer und partizipativer Angebote.

Sie fördern die Zusammenarbeit mit Schulen, Fachstellen, Vereinen, Institutionen und weiteren Partnerorganisationen und tragen durch gezielte Öffentlichkeitsarbeit zur Sichtbarkeit und Weiterentwicklung der Offenen Jugendarbeit bei. Darüber hinaus verantworten Sie die Budgetplanung und den sorgfältigen Einsatz der finanziellen Mittel der Abteilung.
Unregelmässige Arbeitszeiten sowie Einsätze an Abenden und vereinzelt an Wochenenden gehören punktuell zu dieser Funktion.
Diese Stelle ist für Sie, wenn Sie
* ein Fachhochschuldiplom in Sozialer Arbeit haben oder über eine vergleichbare Ausbildung verfügen.
* mehrjährige Erfahrung in der Offenen Kinder- und Jugendarbeit mitbringen.
* Führungserfahrung oder ausgewiesene Führungskompetenzen besitzen.
* Partizipation mit der Zielgruppe sowie den Mitarbeitenden als selbstverständlich erachten.
* strategisches Denken mit Praxisnähe verbinden können.
* Freude daran haben, Mitarbeitende zu fördern, zu entwickeln und gemeinsam Ziele zu erreichen.
* Erfahrung in der Projektentwicklung und Projektleitung mitbringen.
* über hohe Sozial-, Kommunikations- und Vernetzungskompetenzen verfügen.
* sicher auftreten und unterschiedlichste Anspruchsgruppen adressatengerecht ansprechen können.
* Verantwortung für Finanzen, Budgetierung und Ressourcenplanung übernehmen möchten.
* flexibel sind und die Bereitschaft mitbringen, sich sowohl auf strategischer als auch auf operativer Ebene einzubringen.
Ihre Arbeitgeberin
Die Dienststelle Kinder Jugend Familie ist eine Fachstelle für Kinder und Jugendliche zwischen 6 und 26 Jahren, deren Bezugspersonen und weitere interessierte Erwachsene. Sie übernimmt Aufgaben wie Beratung, Abgabe von Informationen, Unterstützung bei Ideen sowie Begleitung von Angeboten der Freizeitgestaltung.
Die Abteilung Offene Jugendarbeit Zentrum der Dienststelle Kinder Jugend und Familie der Stadt St. Gallen stellt im Stadtzentrum vielfältige Freizeitangebote bereit. Mit Einrichtungen wie der Jugendbeiz talhof, dem Jugendkulturraum flon, den flonateliers sowie der Mobilen Jugendarbeit leistet sie einen bedeutenden Beitrag zur Jugendkultur in St. Gallen.
Unsere Unternehmenskultur
Sie arbeiten in einem wertschätzenden Klima, welches geprägt ist von gegenseitigem Vertrauen, Respekt und Loyalität. Unsere Mitarbeiterinnen und Mitarbeiter fördern wir aufgrund ihrer individuellen Fähigkeiten und Ressourcen.
Das bieten wir
Die Stadt St.Gallen unterstützt die Vereinbarkeit von Beruf, Familie und anderen Lebensbereichen. Daher bieten wir flexible Arbeitsmodelle und familienfreundliche Zulagen. In unserem internen Weiterbildungsprogramm finden Sie interessante Angebote für Ihre berufliche und persönliche Entwicklung.

JUUL Labs is seeking a multifunctional Manufacturing Operations Program Manager to join our Global Supply Chain team. This hybrid role bridges day-to-day contract manufacturing execution with strategic, end-to-end supply chain management.
The mission of this role is to ensure we build products at the right speed (time to market), right price (fully burdened cost), right capacity, and right flexibility to meet the company's growth needs. Acting as a critical operational liaison, you will oversee the complete lifecycle of new and existing products across our global supplier network.
Looking for Candidate in Region who can travel to manufacturing site in Cookeville, TN as needed.

Time to Market & Operational Execution
Launch Optimization: Optimize product supply chains for speed to successfully meet market demand and product launch timelines.
Lead Time Reduction: Work closely with product development and manufacturing teams to minimize lead times while maintaining strict quality standards.
Day-to-Day Oversight: Interface daily with suppliers to manage operational execution, focusing heavily on On-Time Delivery (OTD), Overall Operational Effectiveness (OOE), and forecast execution.
Cost Management & Financial Acumen
Fully Burdened Cost Tracking: Manage total product supply chain costs to ensure the fully burdened price (including material, labor, overhead, and logistics) directly aligns with corporate profitability margins.
Should-Cost Strategy: Partner with finance and engineering to build aggressive should-costs and clear capital expenditure forecasts.
Commercial Negotiations: Negotiate with key suppliers to secure favorable pricing, tooling/equipment budgets, and business terms without compromising product quality.
Capacity Planning, Flexibility & Scalability
Constraint Mitigation: Evaluate production constraints and manage global manufacturing capacity to seamlessly support current volumes and future product roadmaps.
Ramp & Scale Planning: Collaborate with manufacturing partners on staffing, facility foot printing, and equipment allocation to ensure infrastructure is scalable for company growth.
Adaptability: Implement flexible supply chain strategies capable of responding rapidly to market fluctuations, operational bottlenecks, and demand shifts.
Supplier Relationship & Risk Management
Strategic Alignment: Build, evaluate, and maintain relationships with critical contract manufacturers and component vendors to align them with JUUL's operational targets.
Contingency Planning: Anticipate vulnerabilities and draft proactive business continuity plans to mitigate risks associated with vendor performance, geopolitical fluctuations, and macro supply disruptions.
Performance Quality: Establish metric scorecards and Clear to Build (CTB) tracking to eliminate post-ramp qualifications and unexpected disruptions.
Cross-Functional Leadership & Continuous Improvement
Primary Liaison: Act as the primary champion and operational advocate across engineering, quality, product management, logistics, and finance.
Process Excellence: Utilize KPIs to actively monitor supply chain performance, using a data-driven "sixth sense" to spark continuous improvement, process modifications, and cost-saving loops.

Experience: 5+ years of global supply chain management or complex manufacturing experience (highly preferred in Consumer Electronics, Medical Device, Aerospace, Automotive, or Pharmaceutical industries).
Leadership & Influence: Proven history of leading and influencing cross-functional matrixed teams and external partners toward aggressive timelines without relying on direct authority.
Strategic Problem Solving: Advanced capability to switch focus between minute operational issues and high-level macro strategies; a self-starter who proactively hunts for issues and implements permanent solutions.
Technical & Cost Knowledge: Deep comprehension of manufacturing cost structures, automation equipment, and design principles, including basic DFMAC (Design for Manufacturing/Assembly/Cost) metrics.
Systems Proficiency: Highly proficient with standard enterprise software alongside solid familiarity with ERP and supply chain management systems.
Communication Style: Outstanding verbal and written presentation skills with the poise to navigate complex commercial discussions and articulate clear status reports to executives.
Global Travel: Open to traveling globally between 5% and 10% as required.
Required: Bachelor’s degree in Operations Manufacturing, Engineering, Business, or a closely related field.

Technische Projektleitung von A bis Z: Du verantwortest Neu\- und Umbauprojekte von Anlagen, Systemen oder Baugruppen am Standort Istighofen von der ersten Idee über die Ausschreibung und Realisierung bis hin zur finalen Abschlusskontrolle hinsichtlich Leistung, Qualität, Terminen und Budget.
